  "answer": "Several approaches have been proposed to reduce the risk of image classifiers giving unreliable answers on unfamiliar or maliciously altered images, relying on the following mechanisms:

- **Withholding uncertain outputs:** Programs can be designed to indicate uncertainty or completely refrain from providing an output when they are uncertain about a classification (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/dYHiMeSdLrrX3cy4a/embedding-safety-in-ml-development) (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hWb09uq6Zlk).
- **Conservative ensembles:** Systems can be made conservative by requiring two or more different kinds of classifiers to agree before outputting a classification (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hWb09uq6Zlk).
- **Anomaly detection:** Anomaly detectors can be used to warn human operators of potential hazards (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/AwMb7C72etphiRvah/unsolved-ml-safety-problems) or to detect dangerous situations and actively stop the AI system from being used in those scenarios (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/CRMhhnKs7bymY4kbb/my-thoughts-on-the-ml-safety-course).
- **Adversarial training:** To defend against adversarial alterations, model robustness can be improved by introducing perturbations to the training data and conducting further training on those perturbed examples (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/CRMhhnKs7bymY4kbb/my-thoughts-on-the-ml-safety-course).
- **Smoothed Vision Transformers (ViTs):** To defend against maliciously designed adversarial patches, certified defenses use ViTs as the backbone of a derandomized smoothing defense. This mechanism exploits the token-based nature of attention modules used in ViTs to gracefully handle the ablated images used in the defense (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.07719)."
